leads.title: Journal Officiel - Loi du 18 novembre 2016 (effective 1 January 2017)
leads.documents: Transgender legal gender change in France (applies in Réunion as overseas department) without surgery/sterilization requirement, via court order; first-name change via registry office
leads.detail: Voted Senate 6 Nov 2015, National Assembly 24 May 2016, modified 12 July 2016, Senate 28 Sept, Assembly 12 Oct, Constitutional Council ruled constitutional 17 Nov, signed 18 Nov, published Journal Officiel next day

leads.title: French Penal Code, Article 225-1
leads.documents: Bans discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.detail: 1985 law for sexual orientation; July 2012 added 'sexual identity'; Law of 18 November 2016 replaced 'sexual identity' with 'gender identity'

leads.title: French Labour Code (Code du travail), Chapter 2
leads.documents: Employment protections banning exclusion, sanction, dismissal or discriminatory measure on sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.detail: Quoted text lists origin, gender, morals, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, family situation, etc.

leads.title: Constitutional Council Rulings - 17 May 2013 and 17 November 2016
leads.documents: Upheld constitutionality of same-sex marriage law (promulgated 18 May 2013, published Journal Officiel next day) and transgender gender-marker law
leads.detail: Senate approved marriage bill 12 April (179-157 on first article 9 April); Assembly 23 April; challenge by UMP; first ceremony 29 May Montpellier

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - B. vs France (1992)
leads.documents: Court ruling that required France to allow legal gender change after decades-long legislative ban, despite medical/surgical transition
leads.detail: Cited as ending ban; prior 1959 change for Coccinelle with lawyer Robert Badinter, then ban until 1992 case

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Report 2022 on France
leads.documents: Human-rights assessment documenting lack of self-determination, extended waiting times, inequitable geographic access for gender-affirming healthcare; recommends informed consent model
leads.detail: 2022 report; notes ALD 31 coverage by Sécurité Sociale and 2010 decree removing gender identity disorder diagnosis

leads.title: DILCRAH - Interministerial Delegation for the Fight Against Racism, Anti-Semitism, and Anti-LGBT Hatred
leads.documents: French government rights machinery for anti-LGBT hatred; 2022 controversy over scientific committee president membership in The Little Mermaid Observatory
leads.detail: Observatory described gender-affirming care as 'mutilation'; one committee member resigned, president stepped away

leads.title: Police / Interior Ministry figures reported 16 May 2020
leads.documents: Enforcement data on homophobic and transphobic attacks/insults in France (+36% in 2019, ~1,870 victims vs ~1,380 in 2018)
leads.detail: Released right before International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia; follows Macron Oct 2018 condemnation of homophobic violence

leads.title: Law of 31 December 2004 and Law on Freedom of the Press of 29 July 1881, Title 3 Arts 20-21
leads.documents: Hate-crime/speech machinery: criminalizes homophobic injury, defamation, incitement; increased penalties for assault/murder motivated by sexual orientation; created Haute autorité de lutte contre les discriminations et pour l'égalité
leads.detail: Max €45,000 fine and/or 12 months imprisonment; first conviction Jan 2006 of MP Christian Vanneste, later cancelled by Court of Cassation; 2017 transphobia added as aggravator for all imprisonable crimes

leads.title: Overseas Departments and Territories section - applicability to Réunion
leads.documents: Confirms same-sex marriage legal in all overseas departments including Réunion, but lower acceptance, more religious/family-honor context; documents Réunion deputies vote on 2013 law
leads.detail: 11 overseas for including 3 from Réunion, 11 against including 2 from Réunion, 1 Réunion deputy absent; 2014 study: ~20% overseas saw homosexuality as sexuality like any other vs 77% metropolitan France
